rows.name: Nong Khon Kwang, Thailand
rows.description: Tornado devastates homes in Udon Thani. At 2:30 PM on July 24th, a large Tornado swept from the Udon Thani-Nong Khai bypass intersection southeast, passing through the Nong Khon Kwang sub-district in Mueang district. It caused damage to power poles, power lines, traffic signs, advertising signs, and houses in Ban Che, Ban Nong Hin, and Ban Udom Phatthana, Nong Khon Kwang sub-district. Several people were injured, crushed by falling house pillars, and taken to Prachak Silpakom Military Hospital. Widespread power outages occurred. House number 41, Moo 3, Ban Che, Nong Khon Kwang sub-district, was completely destroyed; the roof and walls were blown away, leaving only the pillars, floor, and water jars. The roof structure was blown 100 meters away, and corrugated iron sheets were blown over 1 kilometer away. Most notably, a large tractor-trailer carrying hundreds of kilograms of agricultural equipment was blown away. The house was blown over and landed upside down in a rice field about 60 meters away. A twin-tub washing machine was also blown away and severely damaged, landing about 50 meters from the house. Mr. Sawat Banthao, 42, the homeowner, revealed that at the time of the incident, he was at work taking care of his shop. His wife, Mrs. Jirapha Banthao, 42, was at home helping neighbors plant rice. When he learned that the house had been damaged by the wind, he rushed back and found villagers helping his wife, who was trapped under a fallen house pillar, to be taken to the hospital. He recounted that when the wind blew, his pickup truck was parked in front of the house. When the wind came, he saw it nearby and ran to hug a pillar, but before he could reach it, the pillar broke and fell on his leg. He remained there until the storm subsided, at which point villagers helped him free. Mr. Samran Kanha, 38, a neighbor at house number 41/1, Moo 3, Ban Se, revealed that while the storm was passing through his house, about 100 meters from the damaged house, he looked out the window and saw a storm resembling a "tornado" like those seen in Western movies. It had a radius of about 30-40 meters, was black, and swirled very violently. The storm moved rapidly, preceded by strong winds followed by a whirlwind, leaving behind damage. Mr. Krit Rittilee, Mayor of Nong Khon Kwang Municipality, revealed that he personally surveyed the damage. Initial findings indicate a radius of approximately 100 meters along the storm's path, with the most severe damage affecting six houses in Ban Se, three houses in Ban Nong Hin, and two houses in Ban Udom Phatthana. One person was injured. The municipality has dispatched staff to provide immediate assistance. Tomorrow, they will expedite the assessment of the damage and provide assistance according to regulations. Mr. Samak Chanthasarn, a Level 9 engineer from the Provincial Electricity Authority, Udon Thani, stated that the storm blew several materials onto a 15 kV high-voltage power line supplying electricity to the Non Sung and Pak Dong substations. The damage is estimated at approximately 100,000 baht, but it was necessary to cut off power to switch to a new transmission line, which was resolved about an hour after the incident. Repairs to the damaged electricity at the Udon Thani-Khon Kaen bypass intersection, which supplies traffic lights before entering Udon Thani city, will be completed today.

rows.description: Fragmented multiple vehicles to unrecognizable pieces (or otherwise just outright granulated them) and threw said pieces miles, including a firewall of a 1978 Ford pickup (owned by the Hiatt family) being found 7 miles from its point of origin. Combines were also fragmented, with their resulting pieces being thrown extreme distances. Multiple homes were swept cleanly, with debris being removed fully from the foundations of multiple farmsteads, and nearby trees being fully debarked, denuded, and I would assume stubbed. A 26-foot-wide, 3-foot-deep hole was carved into the ground by the tornado, which would not have been caused by debris impact or prior rainfall in the region loosening the soil. Other areas were trenched, as well. The tornado itself formed in an extreme, boundary-dependent environment, and had very high MLCAPE and SFCCAPE values.

Elie, MB, Canada
rows.description: On June 22, 2007, around 6PM, a rope-like tornado would touch down north of the Trans-Canada Highway and Elie, Manitoba. The tornado veered southeast as it approached the highway then shifted due south as it reached proximity of the highway. As it crossed the highway, it shifted southeast then moved due south once again as it looped over a grain elevator, causing its first instance of damage. As it finished the loop it continued to move south before making a hard turn towards Elie, causing intense damage to the Godin Household and three other homes. As it looped once again over the homes, it turned to the southwest before finally dissipating.

rows.name: Roanoke, IL
rows.description:
Supercell thunderstorms tracked across northern and central Illinois the afternoon and evening of July 13, 2004.  A violent tornado tracked for 9.6 miles across Woodford County, with the tornado reaching F4 intensity along a 1-mile stretch between Metamora and Roanoke.

Damage surveys were completed by National Weather Service and Woodford County ESDA personnel on July 14 and 15.  Specific details on the tornado's track follows.

The tornado touched down approximately 1.8 miles north of Metamora, a few hundred yards southeast of the intersection of Illinois Route 89 and county road 1600N.  The tornado was initially of F0 (40-72 mph) strength.  It moved southeast, and strengthened to F2 intensity (113-157 mph) near the time it reached county road 1300E.  It then began a temporary eastward movement for about a half mile, before curving southeast again.  It crossed Route 116 just west of the Route 117 junction, and was at F3 strength (158-206 mph) at this point.

The tornado increased to F4 intensity (approximately 210-240 mph) as it crossed Route 117, demolishing the Parsons Manufacturing Plant at this intersection.  Approximately 140 people were in the plant at the time, but all made it to storm shelters in time (approximately 3-5 minutes before the tornado arrived).  Steel beams and metal siding from the plant were found approximately 3/4 mile east in a farm field.

From the plant, the tornado continued east, just south of Routes 116/117, affecting 4 farmsteads approximately 1/2 to 1 mile east of the plant.  Two of the farmsteads closest to the plant (about 1/2 to 3/4 mile east) had the 2-story houses completely blown away, with only debris remaining in the basements and nearby property.  The other two farmsteads had significant damage to the 2-story houses, with outbuildings demolished.  The center of the tornado's track was about 100 yards south of the farmsteads on the south side of the highway.

From the plant to the farmsteads, the storm was F4 intensity.  The average width of the tornado during this time was 400 yards, and was close to 1/4 mile wide at times. 

At this point, the tornado began to travel in a more east-southeast direction, and caused significant damage to a barn near the intersection of county roads 1300N and 1700E. It caused significant damage at a farmstead at the southeast corner of 1300N and 1800E.  The tornado crossed 1300N shortly afterward, and lifted around 2:57 pm about 2.5 miles southeast of Roanoke, at county road 1900E.

The tornado was on the ground for approximately 23 minutes.

rows.name: Marion, ND
rows.description:
On July 18, 2004, a supercell thunderstorm tracked across southeast North Dakota and making a F4 tornado that tore a 12-mile path through Barnes and LaMoure counties. The storm completely blindsided weather models because the cloud bases were unusually high, but extreme summer heat mixed with intense humidity from local crops created a volatile environment. Strong wind shear quickly forced the supercell into a tight, highly destructive column that pushed hard to the south southeast.
The tornado hit its peak with winds between 215 and 219 mph, leaving behind some of the most impressive damage ever documented on Marion history. The core of the vortex took direct aim at the Noot family farmstead, totally erasing two multi story homes down to their foundations and shredding 20 steel grain silos. The winds ripped a heavy steel safe right out of a concrete basement floor and threw it a mile away into an open field. A loaded semi truck was tossed 250 yards, heavy tractors were mangled, and 49 cattle were killed on the property.
The most severe damage was done directly to the ground. The tornado completely vacuumed the earth, leaving a 700-yard-wide trench of deep ground scouring where grass, crops, and topsoil were ripped away 8 inches deep into the clay.I did believe that this tornado was absolutly had a place at top 40-20.Thanksfully, nobody was killed or injured in this incident

rows.name: Akçamezra, Turkey
rows.description:
This intense and damaging tornado first touched down at 3:10 p.m. TRT, near the Turkish border just southeast of Ayyasha. The tornado was initially weak causing light damage in fields, the tornado then rapidly intensified to IF2 strength when it moved north into town causing significant damage to roofs and walls to buildings with power lines and utility poles being significantly bent or collapsed. As the tornado moved into the northern part of town, it collapsed a free-standing wall and debranched trees. The tornado then began moving northeast intensifying to IF3 strength as it debarked and completely debranched many mature pistachio trees. The tornado then weakened to IF2.5 strength as it traveled near the town of Silsileh where numerous large trees sustained heavy damage, with many being uprooted, snapped, or debranched. The tornado then impacted the western side of Silsile where there was significant damage done to vegetation and structures, with many structures losing their roofs and walls.

The tornado then crossed the border into Turkey becoming more pronounced and maintaining its significant IF2.5 intensity as it impacted the town of Çangallı, Turkey where masonry buildings were damaged with roofs being heavily damaged, power lines were downed, and a transmission tower collapsed. Pistachio trees in this area also sustained major damage. As the tornado continued on its northeastward path it barely missed the town of İnkılap when the tornado started turning northwest in an attempt to occlude only to fail doing so resulting in the tornado doing a loop in a field near the village. For the next 1.5 km (0.93 mi) of the tornadoes path northwest of Üçdamlar. The tornado began rapidly shrinking, going from almost 800 m (870 yd) wide to only 200 m (220 yd) wide as it was near Çaybeyi that the tornado intensified to IF3–IF4 strength as it completely swept three farm buildings off of their foundations with one of them being thrown 100 m (110 yd) being obliterated upon impact. The tornado then also scoured the ground leading to a sandpapering affect on mature pistachio trees causing extraordinary damage. Numerous trees were also denuded with few being completely debarked, and some others being ripped out of the ground and lofted short distances.

Continuing north, the tornado shrunk again, this time down to 100 m (110 yd) as it impacted the village of Akçamezra, across the village, the tornado destroyed masonry homes, collapsed utility poles, with some trailers/semi-trucks being thrown/overturned along with more structures sustaining significant damage. The core of the narrow IF3–IF4 strength tornado showed at the southeastern side of the village, three masonry homes were completely destroyed, but one in particular with 50 cm (20 in) thick walls having ~60% of the structures walls collapsed. A nearby car was also picked up and thrown 15–20 m (16–22 yd) by the tornado as it debarked more trees, destroyed utility poles, and completely destroyed another masonry home. The tornado weakened slightly to IF2.5 strength as the tornado tracked through the eastern part of the village before quickly reintensifying to IF3 strength as it impacted many farmhouses just on the outside of the village. Several farmhouses received major damage with one of them being nearly completely destroyed besides one wall standing, the farmhouse was well constructed with around 30–40 cm (12–16 in) thick walls.

The tornado continued, moving through rural areas mainly causing damage to crops before weakening to IF2 strength and moving into the eastern side of Kayacık where it damaged the roofs of farm buildings and crossing a highway. A van driving on the highway was thrown into a nearby field injuring both occupants, the tornado continued in that field weakening again to IF1 intensity as it damaged trees and some more farm building roofs south of Karadibek. Eyewitnesses captured the tornado roping out where it lightly damaged crops and then finally dissipated at 3:40 p.m. TRT over some hills near the village.

rows.name: Peoria - Germantown Hills - Toluca, IL
rows.description: (hypothetical) This Violent Tornado touched down around 4:35 PM local time a few miles southwest of General Wayne A. Downing International Airport and rapidly begun propagating east-northeastward, producing EF1-2 damage to airport hangars, before rapidly swelling to about 3/4 of a mile wide, with a visible multiple-vortex structure. The tornado then shifted slightly more northeast, entering downtown Peoria. EF3-4 damage to numerous homes occurred on the southwestern side of town, before completely destroying numerous businesses along and west of Peoria Lake at EF5 intensity. around 22 fatalities occurred in Peoria. The tornado then passed over the U.S 150 bridge, collapsing and twisting the central portion of the bridge, and lofting numerous cars. as the tornado continued northeastward, it would run mostly along highway 116. The tornado, now exceeding 1 1/2 miles wide, would impact eastern portions of Germantown Hills, producing EF4-5 damage to a few well-built homes. As the tornado moved northeastward, it struck a few homes north of Metamora, producing EF3-4 damage to a small development north of Metamora, where 3 people would be killed. As the tornado continued, it would pass over mostly rural fields, slowly taking a northward turn. The tornado would do sporadic EF3-4 damage to rural farmsteads, and would produce a nearly 1-mile-wide swath of ground scouring, with trenching up to 8-10 inches deep in some spots. asphalt roads were scoured away as well in this area. about 3 miles south-southwest of Toluca, the tornado would shrink rapidly to about 1/2 a mile wide, and continue to take a northward turn. The tornado rapidly entered the southern side of Toluca, where the worst damage would be documented. multiple train cars would be lofted at EF5 intensity, and railroad tracks would be bent and twisted by incredibly violent winds. multiple cars were reportedly carried within the outer vortex of the tornado before being lofted between 1/4 of a mile and over 1 mile away from the tornado. Debris from homes in the direct path was granulated and windrowed into nearby fields, and a small suction vortex ripped a tornado shelter, with 4 occupants inside, completely apart, killing all 4 occupants. 13 more people were killed in various structures impacted in Toluca. the tornado then began to rapidly weaken and occlude, taking a north-northwestward turn before dissipating 5 miles north of Toluca. in all, 42 fatalities and 102 injuries would occur in this tornado, and around $1.3 billion in damage occurred.

rows.name: Nghĩa Hưng - Yên Khánh, Vietnam
rows.description: Spawned by Typhoon Bualoi, this violent tornado completely destroyed a reinforced billiard hall at peak EF4 intensity, est. winds of 170-175mph (Formula est. at 195mph). 4 were killed, along 25+ injuries.

rows.name: Tuscany, Italy
rows.description: An extremely violent tornado mainly documented by Machiavelli occurred on August 22, 1456. It originally formed as a tornadic waterspout that came ashore near Ancona, Italy, crossing rural Tuscany, dissipating off the coast of Pisa, Italy after traveling over 260 kilometers (it could've been a family of tornadoes, although this is not confirmed by any source.) Apparently, it also had a width of 3.2 kilometers, making it one of the widest tornado events on record. The tornado fully debarked large oak trees, leveled farmer homes and 2+ meter thick villas (likely made of reinforced masonry,) dug "trenches," displaced trees/church roofs for kilometers, and threw debris up to 25 kilometers away. In the aftermath of the devastating whirlwind, 20 were killed, and 6 were injured. Note: this event may be exaggerated/unreliable due to its old age and the author of the main source being born after it happened.

rows.name: Ovilla, TX
rows.description: On December 26th, 2015, an intense, small tornado would tear across the Dallas suburbs of Midlothian, Ovilla, Red Oak, Oak Leaf, and Glenn Heights, Texas. This tornado would be on the ground for 13 minutes, injure 46, and earn a rating of EF3/160MPH.

rows.name: Camden, NJ
rows.description:
An extremely violent tornado struck Camden around
3 PM, obliterating the extensive chemical works of
Messrs. Potts and Klett. The disaster resulted in three fatalities and injuries. The newly completed building, situated on Cooper's Creek along Haddon Ave., between Line and Pine Streets, approximately one mile north of Camden, had been deemed structurally sound by experienced architects. It was a two-story brick structure, 200 feet long and 36 feet wide. Its walls were an impressive 22 inches thick, reinforced with internal and external pilasters for added strength. The primary girders, measuring 12 by 16 inches, were double-bitted and supported by posts of the same size. These girders rested on interior pilasters. Throughout the structure, white pine joists, each 3 by 14 inches and spaced 9 inches apart, were reinforced with truss-bridging.
The roof was covered in slate and featured a surrounding gallery, indicating that no expense had been spared in making it a robust and
comprehensive establishment. During the Coroner's inquest, a master carpenter and a bricklayer provided sworn testimony regarding the structural integrity of the building. A detailed plan of the building was presented and explained, with dimensions as previously reported. Both witnesses affirmed that the highest quality materials were utilized in its construction, which, in contrast, was compensated on a daily basis. The total cost amounted to approximately $10,000 (CP| Adjusted $387,310). All witnesses concurred that exceptional care had been taken to ensure the building's
strength and safety, reflecting its inherent character.
At the time of the tornado, Messrs. Potts and Klett, along with their bookkeeper, were in a small office partitioned off in the northern section of the building. Six laborers were engaged in clearing debris elsewhere in the facility, preparing for machinery installation. Those inside the building were first alerted by a violent clap of thunder,
accompanied by lightning and a hailstorm. The shock was so severe it felt as if the building was shaken to its core. Simultaneously, the entire structure, excluding its northern end, was torn from its foundation and rotated almost completely from southeast to northwest before being carried away and shredded, the debris being scattered in a semicircular pattern. The laborers, fearing entrapment, leapt from the windows, only to be struck by falling sections of the heavy walls. The three men killed instantly were Anthony Schwab, a
24-year-old German; Augustus Bronte; and James Darey. Three others sustained minor injuries. The tornado, which lasted only a few minutes, twisted off numerous large trees and destroyed several
smaller buildings
oss a two-mile stretch. The
immense noise it generated was audible from a significant distance. Gentlemen driving on Haddon Ave., about a mile from the chemical works, reported that upon hearing the initial thunderclap, they observed what appeared to be a revolving pillar of fire in the sky, immediately followed by the sound of the building's walls collapsing.

Monette - Leachville, AR - Hayti, MI - Samburg, TN
Greensburg, KS
rows.description:
Greensburg, KS EF5 | 04 May 2007.

If there is any important instance/example of damage that I am missing, please feel free to tell me. I will add it to this list.

Structural Damage

FR12 | DOD10 | EXP-UB = >200-205 MPH for four residences south of Greensburg proper, up-close videos and imagery show the presence of anchor bolts with nuts, washers, and properly applied sill plates.

EF5 rating assigned to 7 homes in total, 5 of which were in Greensburg proper.

Greensburg high school - triple-wythe unreinforced masonry walls sustained collapse. An MBS structure appendage to the school also sustained damage. Personal estimate: ~195 MPH. Tim Marshall alluded to this structure as being "close to EF5".

95% of Greensburg proper damaged or destroyed.

The Greensburg Mennonite Church, a large, brick masonry church, was reduced to rubble.

Some foundations in Greensburg may have allegedly suffered damage.

Vegetation

Hardwood trees in and surrounding Greensburg were fully debarked, denuded, and in some cases stubbed (reduced to bare stumps).

Projectiles, in some cases silverware and sheet metal, were embedded deeply into debarked trees.

Vehicles

Multiple vehicles were violently pancaked, flattened, mutilated, mangled, shredded to unrecognizable pieces, fragmented, etc.

In one instance, a silver pickup truck was thrown ~1 mile, with only the smashed front frame of the truck recovered.

Object Displacement

Multiple large steel tanks, originating ~7 miles south of Greensburg, were found deposited in Greensburg proper, having been carried by the circulation the entire distance. Most of these tanks were mangled or extremely battered.

Heavy farm machinery was displaced extreme distances and mangled, including a combine.

Other

A segment of railroad tracks north of Greensburg was bent by the tornado.

Extreme powderization/atomization of debris - most apparent in the 4 homes swept south of Greensburg.

A poorly constructed home in Greensburg proper was so annihilated that it was described as 'trenched'.

Manhole covers were uprooted in Greensburg.

Scouring several inches deep in loam soil occurred south of Greensburg.

Highest radar-indicated Vrot of any EF5 tornado. Occurred in one of the most intense tornadic environments ever recorded.

A persistent "hole" in precipitation in the core of the tornado was noted on radar - an extremely rare occurrence, suggesting a ridiculously violent and mature core.

Windrowing of debris occurred up to 0.25-0.5 miles away from the core of the tornado.

- Manitoupoet (https://www.reddit.com/r/tornado/comments/1t4z5up/everything_you_need_to_know_about_the_damage_from/)

rows.name: Tyler, ND - Doran, MN
rows.description:
A violent tornado that touched down south-southwest of Tyler, North Dakota. As the tornado moved east-northeast, it carve deep scour marks into the earth, before striking a farmstead at EF3 intensity west of the North Dakota and Minnesota border. A home and a shelter-belt of trees were severely damaged at the farmstead. Another shelter-belt of trees were debarked as it crossed into Minnesota. Low-end EF4 damage southwest of Doran, Minnesota as it maintained a "drillbit" formation and continued to carve apparent scour marks into the earth.

Crossing into Minnesota, intensifying to low-end EF4 intensity, completely sweeping away seven well-built farm buildings and severely damaging a home. Major tree damage was noted to the shelter-belt surrounding the farmstead. A Ford pick-up truck was thrown half a mile with its engine block ripped out of the frame. Very heavy scouring was noted to a sugar-beet field in this area, with beets being yanked out of the ground. Peak wind speeds in this area were estimated to be 175 mph (282 km/h). The tornado continued for about a mile and soon dissipated southwest of Doran.

rows.name: Caviness - Mid City, TX - Sawyer, OK
Wette'e, Sidrap, Indonesia
rows.description:
The afternoon of February 24, 2012, a severe convective storm developed over the South Sulawesi peninsula. A violent, highly compressed anticyclonic tornado touched down and tracked across a portion of the Sidrap Regency, reaching an estimated high-end EF3 intensity along its core path through the Panca Lautang district.
Damage surveys and local assessments were conducted following the event. Specific details on the tornado's track and impact follow.
The tornado touched down at approximately 3:00 PM local time in the vicinity of Wette'e Village. The vortex was initially compact but rapidly intensified as it moved through the residential area. The storm was on the ground for approximately 15 minutes, carving a localized but devastating path of destruction.
The tornado reached its peak intensity—estimated by severe weather analysts to be at least a high-end EF3 (winds of 140–165 mph)—as it tore directly through the heart of the village. The violent winds completely demolished 47 traditional wooden and semi-permanent homes, flattening them entirely to their footprints. Another 12 homes sustained significant structural damage.
Tragically, 4 people were killed and over 60 others were injured by flying debris and collapsing structures as the vortex hit. Approximately 215 residents were left entirely displaced.
Along the path of peak intensity, the tornado exhibited extreme surface-grasping behavior. Ground surveys noted severe denuding and deep debarking of hardwood trees, with limbs completely stripped away. The core of the funnel also caused intense ground scouring and heavy mud-blasting across the impacted zone, indicating exceptionally high velocity winds right at ground level.
After tearing through the residential sector of Wette'e, the tornado rapidly weakened and lifted, leaving behind a narrow trail of pulverized debris and intense vegetation damage.

rows.name: Preng, Thailand
rows.description:
Residents of Samut Prakan were left reeling after a rare tornado struck on October 12, tearing through homes in Moo 3, Preng Subdistrict, Bang Bo District, leaving five houses damaged, three heavily. Locals described the violent winds as the worst they had ever seen in 70 years. Video footage captured household items swirling into the air as the tornado struck, illustrating the storm’s terrifying power.
Meanwhile, in Angthong Province, elderly residents continue to struggle with prolonged flooding. Noy, 85, has been living atop elevated platforms inside her partially submerged home in Thewarat Subdistrict, Chaiyo District, as floodwaters nearly reached the second floor. Though water levels have slightly receded, the risk of structural damage to her wooden house remains. Local volunteers and relatives are providing food and assistance, but uncertainty persists over when the flooding will end.
Elderly residents in Angthong continue to cope with high floodwaters, relying on relatives and volunteers for essential supplies.
According to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM), 15 provinces remain affected by flooding, including Phitsanulok, Sukhothai, Phichit, Nakhon Sawan, Uthai Thani, Chai Nat, Sing Buri, Angthong, Suphan Buri, Ayutthaya, Pathum Thani, Nakhon Pathom, Ubon Ratchathani, Udon Thani, and Chachoengsao. Across these provinces, 116,043 households and 387,568 people have been impacted.
Authorities continue to operate rescue teams and deploy heavy machinery to aid affected communities. Relief measures include a financial assistance program of 9,000 baht per household, with provinces tasked to survey damages and prepare for immediate disbursement once funds are allocated.

It formed on 6/23/2011 around 17:20-17:30 PM UTC +7, it heavily damaged houses, debarked trees and torn a car (unidentified model) apart. It killed a pregnant woman and injured 80 people. It formed as a drill bit then formed into a wedge. It is argued to be EF4 but the houses in that area isn’t really strong making it stay as EF3.

Parkersburg-New Hartford, IA EF5 | 25 May 2008.

If there is any important instance/example of damage that I am missing, please feel free to tell me. I will add it to this list.

Structural Damage

A total of 17 homes in the tornado's path were assigned EF5 ratings, the maximum-rated structure being rated 205 MPH. 6 of these residences were in Parkersburg proper, whereas 11 were in rural areas (past Parkersburg, New Hartford, etc.)

Upon entering the southwestern corner of Parkersburg proper, the tornado impacted a properly-anchored industrial building, in which the structure was swept bare and metal beams were distorted beyond recognition. Official damage contours show that this structure was rated EF4 - it is a misconception that it was rated EF5.

Multiple homes in the Parkersburg golf course subdivision, east of Parkersburg, were swept bare, with debris finely granulated and windrowed for extreme distances, potentially hundreds to thousands of yards. One of these homes had one of the most textbook structural failures in recent history, as sill plates held down by properly-spaced anchor bolts with nuts and washers were ripped away, with the bolts laterally bent (signifying that the home was extremely well-anchored and failed correctly).

At this same home, a concrete walkout basement wall was pushed over by a combination of debris impact and tornadic winds. Under an idealized situation, Ethan Moriarty calculated this feat to require ~273 MPH winds. The concrete basement walls inside the home (not the same as the walkout basement wall) cracked at the floor-wall joint in at least one location.

In a home near Parkersburg, a rod of #4 rebar was fractured (sheared) at ground level.

A CMU-style home in New Hartford was "trenched" - a fatality was recorded in the basement of this home.

Vegetation

Hardwood trees in Parkersburg with multiple layers of bark suffered partial debarking. Some less-resistant hardwood trees were fully debarked, denuded, and partially ground to stumps.

Between Parkersburg and New Hartford (as well as in New Hartford), large hardwood trees were fully debarked. In one instance, a tree was "shredded" towards the ground, as if the tornado had taken the tree and peeled it outwards in all directions.

Non-debris-impact-induced debarking occurred (debarking trees without debris impact is uncommon).

Trees were uprooted, lofted, thrown, plastered in debris, etc.

Vehicles

Multiple vehicles were thrown hundreds of yards, mangled well beyond recognition, stripped to their bare chassis and embedded in the ground, fragmented into multiple pieces, etc.

A vehicle "graveyard" was constructed for the multitudes of vehicles that were beyond repair.

In the previously-mentioned "trenched" home in New Hartford, a vehicle was thrown hundreds of yards, with the engine block separated from the frame of the vehicle and thrown hundreds of yards in the opposite direction.

One vehicle was reduced to its thin bottom frame (chassis) and tangled in a tree.

Object Displacement

Near a granary site east of Parkersburg, heavy machinery was displaced impressive distances. The large granaries at this site (containing corn) were deformed and deroofed.

As mentioned previously, vehicles were thrown hundreds of yards and mangled well beyond recognition.

Other

Interactions with gravity waves aloft in the atmosphere allowed the Parkersburg supercell to rapidly intensify.

Due to inconsistencies in the damage path and damage contours (EF-ratings at specific locations in the tornado's path), it has been determined that the Parkersburg supercell actually cycled around the Cedar Falls area, and once more near Dunkerton. This has significant implications about the tornado's path length, forward speed, maximum width (which was recorded near Dunkerton - the Parkersburg tornado was likely ~0.8 miles wide), media, and meteorological legacy. (Reference: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3DewcUnD--8&t=851s )

Ridiculously intense cycloidal marks were observed between Parkersburg proper and the granary site. Cycloidal marks were also observed in the other two tornadoes - the famous "S-shaped curve" mark is from the Dunkerton EF2.

In the New Hartford area, a graveyard site was impacted. Besides trees being debarked and shredded and mangled/pancaked vehicles being tangled in shrubbery, gravestones were toppled. Toppled headstones at gravesites have also been observed in the 1985 Niles, OH-Wheatland, PA F5, 1985 Beaver Falls, PA F3, 1979 Windsor Locks, CT F4, and 1974 Xenia-Wilberforce, OH F5.

Pavement was scoured along Highway 57, between Parkersburg and New Hartford.

rows.name: Goessel, KS
rows.description: On March 13th, 1990, the second of a pair of F5 tornadoes would attack Kansas. This particular tornado is most infamous for the footage documenting another tornado--the Hesston F5--merging into it. Unfortunately, however, not much is known about this particular tornado since the Hesston tornado overshadowed it, due, in part, to a direct impact on the northern parts of town. What is known, however, is that Ted Fujita, the man behind tornado science, said himself that it was one of the strongest tornadoes he had ever seen.

rows.name: Wildwood - Lady Lake, Florida
rows.description: First ever officially ranked tornado with the EF scale. Formed on 3:08 AM EST, Stayed on the ground for 17 minutes, Tracked 16-16.5 miles. It killed 8 people, injuring unknown, damaging $114 million (2007 Dollars). It was a violent EF3 having winds around ~150+ MPH  and top winds around 155-160+ MPH.

rows.name: Ringgold, GA - Apison, TN
rows.description: a violent, long-track EF4 tornado that struck northern Georgia and southeast Tennessee on the evening of April 27, 2011, as part of the historic 2011 Super Outbreak.

rows.name: Enderlin, ND
rows.description:
Enderlin train feat is likely ~234 sustained accounting for the fact that the Procor hopper bounced multiple times in its trajectory (EnhancedWx used a mass simulation algorithm to model object displacement like this, and yielded a 234.2 mph average for the feat, not 100% correct), extreme cottonwood lofting + stubbing and bur oak rootball displacement + debarking down to the secondary xylem, hundreds of yards of mature crops stubbed, reportedly sucked a pond dry and pleated its algae into cycloidals.
NTP calculations for the lofted / rolled train car had a range of 266 - 492 mph and a median of 379 mph.

rows.name: La Plata, MD
rows.description:
On the evening of April 28th, 2002, an extremely swift tornado formed near La Plata, Maryland. In the wake of the tornado, 3 people would tragically lose their lives to the multi-vortex tornado, and over 120 other people were injured. The tornado ultimately caused $115 million dollars in losses, and is still known today as one of the strongest storms to hit the area near Washington D.C and Baltimore.

Meteorological Setup
------
The SPC first noted the possibility of organized severe weather across the lower Missouri River Valley on April 25th. At that time, an upper level trough was moving eastward over the United States. The Storm Prediction Center would highlight a moderate risk of severe weather... for the Midwest. Maryland is not in the Midwest, so why wasn't it under any type of risk?

Regardless, just two days later, a coupled jet stream was noted. This was actually quite favorable for severe weather, and in response to this observation, potent 850 mB winds of 70 MPH were measured over Missouri which only enhanced the moisture, which was moving northward. Within the advection of warm air, multiple clusters of elevated atmospheric convection appeared throughout the day, which coincided with steep lapse rates. Thunderstorms were expected to fire in the Great Plains, along the dryline.

An unstable environment did come to being in that particular region, but homographs favored the threat of hailstones and damaging winds from whatever discrete activity before the storms congealed into a squall line overnight.

Meanwhile, in Iowa and Nebraska, there was more of a tornado threat which was expected to evolve along the warm front and to the east of the surface low. Possible storms could even produce F2+ tornadoes. By the afternoon, significant storm activity was observed in northeastern Kansas, northwestern Missouri, and southwestern Iowa. Over the ensuing hours, a few minor tornadoes came and went. 

After the sun set, the biggest severe weather risk moved over into Missouri, all the way east into Ohio. The SPC noted that, because of the isolated nature of potential supercells, they may need to issue a high risk. Various supercells moved across the area, taking advantage of the environment which was rich in storm-relative helicity. Many tornadoes were produced at this time, including significant tornadoes.

But what about Maryland? La Plata is nowhere near the Midwest. Well, on the morning of the 28th, the moderate risk was extended from Ohio all the way to a significant portion of the Mid-Atlantic region, including La Plata. The upper level trough had moved eastward, and was now located over the Ohio Valley. Pre-frontal convection occurred around this point, but was expected to weaken due to the Appalachian Mountains and the stable air around them.

However, a cold front was moving eastward into Pennsylvania. Forecasters feared the formation of a squall line, which posed a risk for hail, damaging winds, and several tornadoes. Large scale forcing was located north of Virginia, but only scattered storms were expected. 

However, one particular supercell formed over West Virginia and it moved to the east, over Virginia. The supercell produced a strong tornado in Shenandoah County. When a boundary lifted at some point, unstable air began entering the once stable area, so the supercell had what it needed to produce a significant tornado, and that was exactly what it did.

The tornado
------

At 6:56 PM, a tornado would form near the community of Marbury. It was quickly making its way towards another small community known as Ripley, which was hit at F2 intensity. A forecaster tried calling officials in La Plata about the tornado, which was being detected on radar, but it took several attempts due to clogged phone lines and other factors. Tornado warnings were soon issued 6 minutes after the tornado formed, but the EAS system encountered various issues. Over half of the radio stations in La Plata were facing issues such as outages that stopped them from getting the alert. Around this time, a second tornado may have formed about 0.25 miles south of the main F4 tornado.  Both tornadoes soon plowed into downtown, devastating the area. The second tornado lifted as the F4 tornado moved through Charles County. The second tornado was rated as an F2. 

The F4 tornado hit the town of Benedict before entering Calvert County at F2 intensity. The tornado moved offshore, narrowly missing a nuclear power plant. At this time, yet another satellite tornado formed. The tornadoes moved over the entire bay and returned onto land at F3 intensity before lifting near Salisbury, Maryland. There have only been 2 other (E)F3 tornadoes in the Delmarva Pennisula. The first one in June 1944, and the other one in April 2023.

The tornado was on the ground for 1h30m, and moved 78 miles. The only other violent Maryland tornado hit in 1998. The tornado also moved at about 52 MPH, so it moved quite quickly. La Plata in particular suffered the brunt of the damage, where about 2/3 of the downtown sustained heavy damage or complete destruction. The tornado was also preliminarily rated as an F5, which would make it the easternmost F5 tornado on record and the only F5 tornado in Maryland. However, it would not be the only F5 tornado in the northeast, because of an F5 tornado in 1985 which struck Niles, Ohio and Pennsylvania.

rows.name: Takhli, Thailand
rows.description: Nakhon Sawan Governor Thanakom Chongchira and representatives of related agencies visited residents in Takhli district Friday and assessed the damage. The Tornado that hit the central province damaged 27 houses and brought down 89 utility poles, causing power outages in the districts of Takhli and Tak Fa and a nearby district in Chai Nat province. Takhli Provincial Electricity Authority estimated the damage to its infrastructure at six million baht and said it would take around three days to restore power supplies in all affected areas. In the North, heavy rains triggered a mudslide and flash floods in several areas in Chae Son sub-district of Lampang province. Civil workers and villagers combined forces to remove a fallen tree and mud that blocked a mountainside road. In the Northeast, days of thundershowers have raised the water levels of the Mekong River. Fishermen in Bueng Kan province have taken the opportunity to catch fish which sell for 200-300 baht per kilogram. Many of them are able to make 1,000- 2,000 baht a day.

rows.name: Chaiya, Thailand
rows.description:
a Tornado hit Surat Thani province after heavy rain throughout the night. The strong winds damaged over 60 houses in villages 1, 2, and 5 of Ban Trakob, Chaiya district, and the Ban Trakob health center. The wind also caused trees to fall, damaging power lines and resulting in a village-wide blackout. The incident caused considerable panic among residents, especially those living near the coast. Thirty families have been evacuated to safer areas. Initially, there were no reports of injuries or fatalities. However, the province has instructed Chaiya district to urgently assess the damage and provide assistance. Currently, Surat Thani province continues to experience continuous rainfall with waves reaching 1-2 meters high. Nakhon Si Thammarat province also experienced heavy rainfall until this morning, causing flooding in low-lying areas and rough seas. Fishing boats, both small and large, in Pak Phanang, Sichon, and Khanom districts are rushing back to shore. Meanwhile, residents in high-risk areas at the foot of mountains in Lan Saka and Phipun districts are concerned about landslides or subsidence. The districts have issued warnings to residents to be vigilant and prepared.
The Nakhon Si Thammarat Provincial Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Office has opened disaster relief centers in all 21 districts and 2 sub-districts. This is due to surveys revealing several vulnerable areas at the foot of mountains in Nakhon Si Thammarat province that are at risk of such incidents. However, they are confident that the current readiness of personnel and equipment from all sectors will be sufficient to cope with the flooding, although concerns remain regarding potential landslides.
